leftEvidence.title: Provision, accusation, and cursing meet David on the road

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Ziba brings supplies and accuses Mephibosheth; David grants property, then Shimei curses and throws stones while David refuses Abishai’s proposal to kill him.
points.right: Hushai greets Absalom, explains his allegiance, and Ahithophel counsels public possession of David’s concubines on the roof.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David makes one quick property judgment and leaves another hostile act to possible divine regard inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the seized city displays a household consequence Nathan had announced inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 2 Samuel 16:1–14 and 2 Samuel 16:15–23 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Exile, Return, and Rebellion” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Absalom enters Jerusalem and receives Ahithophel’s counsel

payload.tension: 2 Samuel 16:1–14 foregrounds David makes one quick property judgment and leaves another hostile act to possible divine regard; 2 Samuel 16:15–23 foregrounds the seized city displays a household consequence Nathan had announced. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
